items.text: REFERRED TO ALCOHOLISM AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to requiring an annual
report for the independent substance use disorder and mental health ombudsman
program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8219

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to requiring an
annual report for the independent substance use disorder and mental
health ombudsman program

 
PURPOSE:

Requires an annual report for the independent substance use disorder and
mental health and ombudsman program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 33.27 of the executive law of independent
substance use disorder and mental health ombudsman to require the
ombudsman to submit a yearly report by December 31st to the governor,
temporary senate president, speaker of the assembly, and necessary
legislative committee chairs providing recommendations for changes on
systemic issues that are discovered during the year.

Section 2 establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2018 the Community Health Access to Addiction and Mental Health
Project (CHAMP) created an ombudsman program helping individuals access
treatment and insurance coverage for the services they require. This
program has been incredibly successful in helping individuals navigate
this complicated system. The CHAMP program can help investigate and
resolve complaints and violations of rights. It represents individuals
and helps advocate for access to treatment, denial of services, access
to medication, parity/coverage, discrimination issues, system naviga-
tion, medical benefits, enrollment referral, legal assistance for insur-
ance appeals.

This bill will ensure more transparency on how well OASAS is able to
identify and resolve issues that consumers have with their coverage
access to continued substance use disorder care by requiring them to
submit a yearly report- with the deadline being December 31st for each
year- that summarizes the work done by the program, and providing
systemic issues that had been discovered during the year.  This will
help ensure that the program is properly supporting these individuals,
and would help reflect if there would be need for program change in the
future.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Fiscal note not attached.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
